result.title: Coherence-Driven Belief Formation and Population Dynamics of Contagion in LLM Agents
result.comment: 18 pages, 6 figures. Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Foundations of Agentic Systems Theory (FAST)
result.summary: Models of social contagion usually assume how individuals adopt beliefs and derive population behavior from it. We instead empirically measure belief adoption in language model agents, quantifying the probability an agent adopts a claim given how many peers endorse it. We find this adoption kernel to be sigmoid, a characteristic of complex contagion, with a threshold that is sensitive to three sources: the claim's plausibility, the source's reliability, and the agent's disposition. These three dimensions are well approximated by a single effective dimension which we propose can be understood as the coherence of the incoming belief with the LLM agent's prior beliefs. Further, we observe a characteristic of complex contagion in the collective dynamics of belief adoption in a system of AI agents: further spread on clustered than random networks. These systems also exhibit a bifurcating cascade window, and self-sustaining hysteretic consensus which lead to consensus being far harder to remove than to establish.

AI.brief_summary: 该研究在语言模型智能体上实证测量信念采纳概率随同伴支持数变化的关系，发现采纳核为带阈值的 S 型曲线，并将可信度、来源可靠性与智能体倾向近似压缩为一个「与先验信念的一致性」有效维度，进而观察聚类网络上的级联与滞后共识等群体动态。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「一致性」强调的新信念与智能体现有状态契合度、以及采纳阈值与信息源筛选，可能与 LVR 中 latent 假设的选择、证据筛选与停止判断存在概念联系，可供核查。
